 Grafton players celebrate with the gold trophy after defeating Reedsburg, 17-15, in the WIAA Division 3 state football championship game at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison on Friday, Nov. 21, 2025. USA TODAY NETWORK The Wisconsin Interscholastic Athletic Association high school football playoffs begin this week with first-round games. The postseason begins with 224 teams whittling down to 14 over the next month that will compete across seven divisions for WIAA state gold balls Nov. 19-20 at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison. Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reporters Zac Bellman and Michael Whitlow gathered their thoughts on the field in each division, providing predictions for sleepers, final four participants and champions. In last year’s predictions, Zac correctly predicted six of the 14 title game participants, 17-of-28 final four picks and three eventual state champions that included one perfect title game prediction of West De Pere over Notre Dame. Michael had five title game participants and 18 final four picks correct, highlighted by a successful prognostication of Arrowhead in the Division 1 state title game.
 Here are their predictions for 2026 across all seven divisions. Division 7
 Bellman: Cochrane-Fountain City ran into a bit of a buzzsaw in Kenosha St. Joseph Catholic last year at Camp Randall, but with the Lancers elevated to D6 this year, the Pirates look like the team to beat in D7. A standout win from their 9-0 regular season is a 21-6 victory over a Pepin/Alma team that could also make a run across the bracket. Ithaca/Weston, in the first year of a co-op, has put together an inspiring campaign on the heels of a tragic loss to their program early in the year. Cashton gave it a run, however, in a 20-14 I/W win earlier this year, and I wonder if an upset could be on the horizon in the second round should there be a rematch. Boyceville was on a run until it encountered C-FC in the sectional final last year, and I see it meeting few equals until such time as those two should rematch in the state semifinal this year. Sleeper pick: Cashton.
 Final four: Cochrane-Fountain City, Boyceville, Pepin/Alma, Lourdes Academy. Title game: Cochrane-Fountain City over Lourdes Academy. Whitlow: It always seems like a good idea to trust the top seeds in this division. More often than not, the No. 1 seeds have been utterly dominant and that’s what this quartet has done in 2026. I do have three of the top four overall seeds advancing with No. 2 Shiocton coming out of Glenwood City’s quarter of the bracket. The Chiefs have a No. 1 seed-worthy resume with four shutout wins and seven victories where their opponents didn’t score more than six points. Still, Coleman feels like the team to beat here. The Cougars hammered Shiocton 42-0 in Week 7 with their two losses coming in Week 2 against No. 1 seed Bonduel (D6) and a blowout defeat to No. 1 seed Amherst (D5). If the Cougars can advance to a potential state semifinal matchup against fellow top-seeded Ithaca/Weston and overcome that last hurdle before Madison, they could be the best team left.
 Sleeper pick: Cashton. Final four: Cochrane-Fountain City, Shiocton, Ithaca/Weston, Coleman. Title game: Coleman over Cochrane-Fountain City.
 Division 6
 Bellman: In a familiar beat of this latest competitive balance era, defending D6 champion Darlington moved up to D5 for this year’s playoffs. The Jerry Sinz-led Edgar Wildcats were the runner-up a season ago and six defensive shutouts this year reflect a team that is bought in for another run at a title. Reigning D7 champion Kenosha St. Joseph Catholic is an enticing No. 2 seed, but I have a hard time seeing a path for the Lancers past top-seeded Manitowoc Lutheran. Mondovi has gotten 37 of its 51 team touchdowns from quarterback Bode Falkner as both a passer and runner, and his efficiency with just three interceptions has also been remarkable while leading the division’s top offense. No. 1 seed Bonduel played No. 2 Kewaunee to a 28-22 Bonduel win on Sept. 4, and I actually like Kewaunee to play a cleaner game and win the rematch in the postseason. Sleeper pick: Randolph/Cambria-Friesland. Final four: Mondovi, Manitowoc Lutheran, Kewaunee, Edgar. Title game: Edgar over Mondovi. Whitlow: I said it last year and I’ll say it again: you can’t bet against Jerry Sinz in October and November. Unless they make the state title game to play the fighting Buffaloes from Mondovi in a Week 4 rematch. Edgar defeated Mondovi 15-8 on Sept. 11 and the Buffaloes have been rolling ever since. They’ve won five straight and earned a No. 1 seed in D6, including a wild 62-57 win over Elk Mound in Week 8. The other two top seeds – Manitowoc Lutheran and Bonduel – are both unbeaten, but haven’t really been challenged much this season outside of a couple games. Edgar’s experience in the postseason with Sinz at the helm, plus Mondovi knowing it could possibly get another crack at the nine-time state champions, makes for an awesome D6 final if we get it. Sleeper pick: Potosi/Cassville. Final four: Mondovi, Manitowoc Lutheran, Bonduel, Edgar. Title game: Mondovi over Edgar. Division 5
 Bellman: The offensive numbers for the top-end D5 teams are eye-popping, and there should be some high-scoring early-round matchups in this bracket. Reigning D5 champion Mayville still looks up for a run at a repeat despite coming into the postseason at 6-3 with a couple losses to quality competition. Should the Cardinals find themselves in a rematch with Amherst, however, I see that going the other way this year. USM quarterback Willy McGregor is dynamic with the ball in his hands and I could see him providing the Wildcats a lift through the first round and maybe an upset of Lake Country Lutheran as well in the second round. Ultimately I see two of the top individual athletes in the division leading their teams to the title game as Amherst running back Ayden Nerdahl leads the Falcons over Cohen Kraus and Racine Lutheran. Sleeper pick: University School of Milwaukee. Final four: Racine Lutheran, Saint Croix Falls, Darlington, Amherst. Title game: Amherst over Racine Lutheran. Whitlow: Darlington surprised many in last year’s postseason with a dominant 42-18 rout of Edgar in the D6 state title game to cap a perfect 14-0 season. The Redbirds are now up in D5 and once again look like one of the best programs in the division with a 9-0 mark and a No. 1 seed. It feels like the top of D5 has a few explosive offenses, including Racine Lutheran, which could make for some exciting games in this bracket. The seven teams that are 8-1 or 9-0 have averaged at least 31.1 points per game, including an absurd 50.8 points per contest from the Crusaders. I think that offense for Racine Lutheran, combined with another dominant run through D5 for Darlington, could set up an awesome title game between the two. Sleeper pick: Chilton. Final four: Racine Lutheran, Saint Croix Falls, Darlington, Amherst. Title game: Darlington over Racine Lutheran. Division 4
 Bellman: Is there any reason to look beyond that first section of the D4 bracket featuring two of the three undefeated teams from the regular season in Freedom and last year’s D5 runner-up Northwestern? What impresses me most with the Freedom Irish is not just the record, but the quality of a couple opponents beaten. Throttled a Lake Mills team that holds a No. 1 seed across the bracket, 40-0 in Week 1. Beat another No. 1 seed in Little Chute, 49-29 in Week 6. Those are two wins that should have the Irish feeling a lot more than lucky with regard to this year’s team. Having the division leader in rushing touchdowns in Axzil Eggert as well as a top-four passing touchdowns leader in Owen Henkel is as good of a one-two punch as you will find across any division. Fellow No. 1 seed Racine St. Catherine’s edged past Shoreland Lutheran 20-13 in Week 8, and I think that is a potential second-round meeting the Pacers could win in a rematch. Sleeper pick: Shoreland Lutheran. Final four: Freedom, Little Chute, Edgewood, West Salem. Title game: Freedom over Edgewood. Whitlow: I’ll be honest: D4 conflicted me like crazy last season. To sum things up more clearly, I didn’t have a single correct final four pick. On top of that, half of the D4 final four – Baldwin-Woodville and eventual state champion Winneconne – are both in D3 this season. I really liked learning about Northwestern prior to its D5 state title game berth last fall and this offense has been just as insane this season in D4. They haven’t played the steepest of competition (36-54 combined opponent record), but they’ve averaged 53.2 points per game, including at least 42 points in every game this season. On the opposite side of the bracket, West Salem feels like Northwestern’s mirror image. Again, the competition hasn’t been the toughest (37-53 combined opponent record), but its point differential is plus-25.3 points (34-8.7) and even in the games it allowed double digits (three times), it scored 42, 43 and 42 points. Sleeper pick: Lodi. Final four: Northwestern, Stratford, Lake Mills, West Salem. Title game: Northwestern over West Salem. Division 3
 Bellman: With three of the No. 1 seeds coming from the Milwaukee area in this bracket, I can definitely see an all-Milwaukee-area final as a possibility for D3. Pewaukee is a team I have seen twice this year, and a punishing run game and hawkish secondary make the Pirates a favorite in my mind for a run this postseason. Section 2 with a Wisconsin Lutheran team that handed Homestead its only loss, a Whitefish Bay team that was the sleeper of last year’s playoffs and a Catholic Memorial team that has had a down year but rarely finds itself out of the conversation in early November will just be a fun group to follow. I anticipate a Port Washington-Plymouth sectional final meeting in Section 3, which Port will have to guard against falling down early in as it did in the regular-season meeting. Fox Valley Lutheran quarterback Braden Heiges has been incredibly tough to slow down due to his lack of reliance on any one receiver, and I think he leads FVL within a breath of the title game in a close state semifinal with Port. Pewaukee quarterback Brooks Dobberstein takes a snap during a game against New Berlin West on Oct. 16 in Pewaukee. The Pirates are a No. 1 seed in Division 3. Sleeper pick: Catholic Memorial. Final four: Pewaukee, Whitefish Bay, Port Washington, Fox Valley Lutheran. Title game: Pewaukee over Port Washington. Whitlow: We start to see a lot more Milwaukee-area flavor in D3 and it feels like the more the playoffs move along, the more area teams will make themselves known. Three of the top four overall seeds – New Berlin West, Pewaukee and Port Washington – have been three of the best programs in the area and across the state all season in D3. Pewaukee has felt like the team to beat as the season moves along with its overpowering offensive line and deep running back depth chart. Another area team has been in that elite tier in Glacier Trails champion Port Washington, which has one of the most exciting offenses in the state. Both teams do it in much different ways, but could absolutely make it an all-area title game next month. Still, don’t sleep on the likes of Catholic Memorial, Wisconsin Lutheran and last year’s Cinderella in Whitefish Bay also making some noise in this field. Sleeper pick: Baldwin-Woodville. Final four: Pewaukee, Wisconsin Lutheran, Port Washington, La Crosse Logan. Title game: Pewaukee over Port Washington. Division 2
 Bellman: One player does not a championship team make, but every so often there comes along a player that takes over a game every time he is on the field. Notre Dame running back and Wisconsin Badgers commit Kingston Allen is that type of player. Last year’s D2 runner-up Tritons only failed to bring home gold in 2025 because they ran into an equally-proficient, record-breaking passing game from West De Pere. Absent that type of threat this year, I expect Notre Dame to run roughshod through the D2 field. Second in D2 by a whopping 21 rushing touchdowns to Allen (48) is New Richmond’s Austyn Wittek (27), who I believe will lead New Richmond to a ground-and-pound D2 title game in which Notre Dame prevails. Allen will make a statement to conclude his all-time greatest rushing career in state history by flashing a “W” hand signal as he scores a putaway fourth-quarter touchdown, letting onlookers at Camp Randall who may be anxious about his recruiting status know he is a Badger once and for all. Sleeper pick: Marshfield. Final four: New Richmond, Marshfield, Notre Dame, Homestead. Title game: Notre Dame over New Richmond. Whitlow: Remember how I said you can’t bet against Jerry Sinz when Edgar is playing in October and November? Well, it feels just as simple here in D2 with No. 1 seed Notre Dame. It has Kingston Allen and the rest of the field doesn’t. The future Wisconsin Badger – at least for now with some top-tier college programs still in pursuit of his services – has been the state’s most dominant player behind a strong and sturdy offensive line with 187 total carries, 2,546 rushing yards and 48 touchdowns in just nine weeks. Also of note, Allen ran 43 times for 242 yards and two scores on his future home field in NDA’s 28-14 loss to West De Pere in last year’s D2 state title game. I’m sure he’d love one more chance to put on a show at Camp Randall in what would be his final high school game. He’s already broken the state’s all-time total touchdown record and could somehow break his own single-season rushing record of 3,436 yards that he set last year with another deep playoff run. He’s only 890 yards behind that mark and he’s already had a game where he surpassed the halfway mark to that number with 458 yards and seven touchdowns against Neenah in the first week of the season. Sleeper pick: Wausau East. Final four: New Richmond, Wausau East, Notre Dame, Homestead. Title game: Notre Dame over New Richmond. Division 1
 Bellman: One of my biggest takeaways from preseason camp visits we did to kick off our 2026 high school football coverage was how heavily a 34-24 sectional final loss to eventual 2025 D1 state champion Arrowhead weighed on the minds of Sussex Hamilton. The Chargers had a 21-0 lead in the first five minutes of that game before watching it slip away, an outcome those that returned were determined to avoid should they get another opportunity. Chalk finishes in Section 3 would set up that rematch in the sectional final, and I have Hamilton knocking off the defending champs this time to guarantee a new champ in 2026. West De Pere may be down a couple Greisens with Patrick graduated and Chris stepping down as head coach, but younger brother Andrew has done just fine leading an undefeated regular season highlighted by a 33-27 victory at fellow No. 1 seed Bay Port. Muskego I nearly wrote off after an unthinkable 19-16 loss at home in Week 5, squandering one of the best stretches at home we have seen anywhere across the state. The Warriors responded with back-to-back road wins at Franklin (31-6) and at Arrowhead (22-20). The defensive front led by Zander Zenisek is dominant, and the Wing-T offensive scheme is crisp and keeps unfamiliar opponents guessing. The Warriors return to glory in head coach Ryan Lucchesi’s first year with the program’s first gold ball since consecutive titles in 2018-2019. Sleeper pick: Marquette. Final four: West De Pere, Muskego, Sussex Hamilton, Bay Port. Title game: Muskego over Sussex Hamilton. Whitlow: Repeat champions in Division 1 used to be a common trend over the last decade-plus. Arrowhead went back-to-back in 2012 and 2013. Kimberly won four straight from 2014 to 2017. Muskego repeated in 2018 and 2019. However, there’s been no repeat champion since the COVID-19 pandemic of 2020. I think that trend continues this postseason. Do I think Arrowhead can win it all again? Absolutely. Its running game and defense is plenty good enough. But, woof. That run through Sussex Hamilton’s quarter of the bracket could wear down the defending champions before Madison. Not only would they have to beat a healthier version of Oconomowoc again in the second round than they saw in Week 6, they could likely face the top-seeded Chargers – a team that had them on the ropes as much as anyone did in last season’s run to the D1 title – in the state quarterfinal round. If the Warhawks clear both of those local hurdles, there’s a potential rematch with a motivated Bay Port bunch that Arrowhead kept from winning back-to-back D1 titles last November. That’s quite a gauntlet of challenges for a team trying to repeat. Also, West De Pere is really, really good. Despite losing both former head coach Chris Greisen and record-setting quarterback son Patrick, Andrew Greisen has stepped into the high-powered WDP offense and led it to the top overall seed in the field. The Phantoms averaged 39.3 points per contest and have allowed opponents to score just 8.4 points per game, while holding a 33-27 win over fellow top seed Bay Port this season. Sleeper pick: Franklin. Final four: West De Pere, Muskego, Arrowhead, Bay Port. Title game: West De Pere over Arrowhead.
